title: Inventory Basics & Systems
description: Understand inventory, cost of goods sold, and periodic vs perpetual systems.
html:
What is inventory?

Inventory consists of goods held for sale to customers or goods used in producing items that will be sold.

For a merchandising company

Inventory usually consists mainly of goods purchased for resale.

Cost of Goods Sold

When inventory is sold, its cost generally becomes Cost of Goods Sold (COGS).

Beginning Inventory + Purchases − Ending Inventory = Cost of Goods Sold

Example

Beginning Inventory $20,000
Add: Purchases $70,000
Goods Available for Sale $90,000
Less: Ending Inventory ($25,000)
Cost of Goods Sold $65,000

Periodic inventory system

Under a periodic system, inventory records are not continuously updated for every sale.

Ending inventory is generally determined using a physical count at period-end.

Perpetual inventory system

Under a perpetual system, inventory records are updated continuously as purchases and sales occur.

Periodic

Inventory and COGS are determined periodically.

Perpetual

Inventory records are updated continuously.

Important

Inventory accounting determines how the total cost of goods available for sale is divided between:

  • Cost of Goods Sold
  • Ending Inventory

quiz.prompt: Beginning inventory is $15,000, purchases are $55,000, and ending inventory is $20,000. What is cost of goods sold?
